{{recipesummary|category=Casserole recipes|servings=6|time=40 minutes|difficulty=3}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Israel|Cuisine of Israel]]

'''Yerushalmi kugel''' is named after the city of Jerusalem. Legend has it that it originated in Jerusalem with the followers of the Vilna Gaon in the 18th century.

==Ingredients==
*8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (200 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Noodle|noodles]] ([[Cookbook:Egg noodles|egg noodles]] are preferred, but others work fine as well)
*⅔ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (160 g) [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] ([[Cookbook:White sugar|white sugar]] is helpful because it's more obvious when it begins to brown)
*4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*1 handful of [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]]
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] noodles according to the package instructions and drain.
#Heat the olive oil in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]], and add ⅓ cup (80 g) sugar.
#Stir continuously until the sugar begins to brown. Remove from heat.
#The sugar will continue to brown for a few more minutes, creating a thick caramel.
#Add the caramel to the noodles.
#Add the sugar, eggs, cinnamon, pepper, and raisins. Stir.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in a pan at 350°F (180°C) until the top begins to brown (about 40 minutes).

steps.text: Boil noodles according to the package instructions and drain.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan, and add ⅓ cup (80 g) sugar.
Stir continuously until the sugar begins to brown. Remove from heat.
The sugar will continue to brown for a few more minutes, creating a thick caramel.
Add the caramel to the noodles.
Add the sugar, eggs, cinnamon, pepper, and raisins. Stir.
Bake in a pan at 350°F (180°C) until the top begins to brown (about 40 minutes).
